topPRs.title: op-dispute-mon: Expand acceptance coverage
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
Builds on ethereum-optimism/optimism#21862.

Expands the dispute monitor acceptance suite across healthy and incorrect SuperPermissioned games, invalid proposal forecasting, reference-node failures, resolved bond accounting, and honest-actor losses. Adds reusable devstack metrics snapshot assertions and the minimal DSL/runtime wiring needed to exercise those scenarios.

Tested all six acceptance scenarios three times on each supported matrix: op-node/op-geth, op-node/op-reth, and kona-node/op-reth. Also ran `go test ./op-dispute-mon/... ./op-devstack/... ./op-service/testlog -count=1` and `mise exec -- just lint-go`.

topPRs.title: docs: add component hub skeleton template + Stack Components section (op-batcher + cannon hubs)
topPRs.author: claude
topPRs.body:
<!-- ccr-slack-attribution -->
_Requested by **Matthew Cruz** · [Slack thread](https://oplabs-pbc.slack.com/archives/C0BHEH8TG91/p1784185257434409)_

Tracks ethereum-optimism/solutions#969

## What

First batch of Option A slice 4 (component hubs) from the canonical-homes plan
(`projects/docs-improver/plans/option-a-canonical-homes.md` in
ethereum-optimism/solutions; program overview: `projects/docs-improver/README.md`):

- **Hub skeleton template** (`op-stack/contribute/component-hub-template.mdx`): the
  uniform section skeleton every component hub follows — Overview → Get started →
  How-tos → Configuration & flags reference → Releases → Source & spec links — with
  per-section guidance. Pattern follows Cloudflare's per-product documentation
  content strategy and ZKsync's zk-stack/components model.
- **Stack Components section** (`op-stack/components/index.mdx` + new nav group in
  the OP Stack tab): one identity page per component, grouped by protocol role. The
  index routes to hubs where they exist and to release history everywhere else.
- **op-batcher hub** (`op-stack/components/op-batcher.mdx`): links the existing
  guide/reference/tutorial/releases surfaces and surfaces the in-repo
  `op-batcher/throttling.md` deep documentation (previously linked from nowhere
  public).
- **cannon hub** (`op-stack/components/cannon.mdx`): cannon's first component home
  anywhere on the site — what it is, who runs it, how it relates to
  kona-client/kona-host and op-challenger, with spec/source/prestate links.

Per the plan, op-batcher (the site's proven guide↔reference pair) and cannon
(previously homeless) ship first; the remaining hubs follow as reviewed batches
tracked on ethereum-optimism/solutions#969.

## Why

Today "where do I find docs for component X" has five different answers depending
on X, and cannon has no component page at all. Hubs give every component exactly
one declared home, per the content guide's canonical-home matrix
(`/op-stack/contribute/content-guide`). Hubs are thin identity-and-links pages:
they link the canonical guide/reference/spec surfaces and never restate them
(dual-sourcing ban).

## Source citations

Every factual claim on the two hubs was verified against monorepo source at
`develop`: `op-batcher/readme.md`, `op-batcher/throttling.md`,
`op-batcher/flags/{flags,types,throttle_flags}.go`, `cannon/README.md`,
`cannon/docs/README.md`, `op-challenger/README.md`,
`scripts/generate-releases.ts` (component one-liners), and the existing
batcher guide/reference pages. Spec links use current (non-`/experimental/`)
specs.optimism.io paths. An independent adversarial accuracy pass re-derived
every claim from source before this PR was opened.

## Nav / redirects (serialized docs.json lane)

This PR occupies the serialized docs.json slot: two minimal hunks (new
"Stack Components" group in the OP Stack tab; template page appended to the
Contribute group). No pages moved or deleted, so no redirects are required.
Checks run locally: nav validator OK, redirect lint OK (no new findings),
link-policy lint zero findings in changed files, docs.json parses.
(`mint broken-links` crash-loops identically on the unmodified develop tree —
pre-existing tool failure, noted for maintainers.)

## Reviewer checklist

- [ ] Both hubs follow the template's exact H2 skeleton (mechanical check)
- [ ] Every hub link goes to the canonical surface (no restated content)
- [ ] Hub overview prose is accurate against `op-batcher/` and `cannon/` source
- [ ] Stack Components group placement in the OP Stack tab reads well
- [ ] Index "Planned" rows are acceptable until the remaining hubs ship

topPRs.title: docs: badge version-pinned links in smart-contracts reference (sweep batch 3)
topPRs.author: claude
topPRs.body:
<!-- ccr-slack-attribution -->
_Requested by **Matthew Cruz** · [Slack thread](https://oplabs-pbc.slack.com/archives/C0BHEH8TG91/p1784185257434409)_

Tracks ethereum-optimism/solutions#962

## What

Sweep batch 3 of the B2 link-policy remediation (follows #21866 and #21867, both unmerged): clears **all 104 `unbadged-pinned-link` findings in `op-stack/protocol/smart-contracts.mdx`** and prunes them from the linter baseline (shrink-only — **368 → 264** entries, key-diff pure removal, 0 added).

Branched from `develop` independently of batches 1 and 2 so all three review in parallel.

## Badge, not re-point

Unlike batch 2 (mostly re-points), every finding on this page is a deliberate release quote: the per-release contract changelogs (`op-contracts/v1.0.0` through `v1.8.0`) that record each contract's semver *at that release*. The pin is the point, so per the [link policy](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/develop/docs/public-docs/op-stack/contribute/link-policy.mdx) each link keeps its pin and gains the policy's "as of `x.y.z`" badge, with the tag taken from the pinned URL itself — including the "No change" rows, which correctly pin *older* tags than the release being described (e.g. `SuperchainConfig 1.1.0` badged `op-contracts/v1.2.0` inside the v1.8.0 changelog). The three commit-sha pins (`LivenessGuard`/`LivenessModule` in v1.5.0, `SystemConfig 2.2.0` in v1.4.0) are badged with the short sha (`9047beb`, `547ea72`).

**Counts: 104 badged, 0 re-pointed, 0 left unbadged.** Two badged entries also get a target correction: the `DeputyGuardianModule` changelog rows in v1.6.0 and v1.5.0 linked `SafeSigners.sol`; they now link `DeputyGuardianModule.sol` at the same tags, with the semver constant verified at each tag (`2.0.0` at `op-contracts/v1.6.0` #L49, `1.1.0` at `op-contracts/v1.5.0` #L47).

## Verification

*   Link-policy linter: 0 new findings, 0 stale with `--specs-src`; `--self-test` green.
*   Baseline key-diff vs `develop`: pure removal (0 added; raw 368 → 264, unique keys 281 → 233).
*   `lint:nav` OK (395 pages, unchanged), `lint:redirects` OK (22 grandfathered, unchanged), `docs.json` untouched.

**Note:** the baseline file conflicts with #21866/#21867 are mechanical; whichever of the three batches merges last re-runs `--update-baseline`.

topPRs.title: docs: badge or re-point version-pinned links (sweep batch 2: guides, tutorials, notices, op-stack references)
topPRs.author: claude
topPRs.body:
<!-- ccr-slack-attribution -->
_Requested by **Matthew Cruz** · [Slack thread](https://oplabs-pbc.slack.com/archives/C0BHEH8TG91/p1784185257434409)_

Tracks ethereum-optimism/solutions#962

## What

Sweep batch 2 of the B2 link-policy remediation (follows #21866, which covered the mechanical classes): works off **95 of the 291 `unbadged-pinned-link` findings** and prunes them from the linter baseline (shrink-only — **368 → 273** entries, key-diff pure removal, 0 added).

Branched from `develop` (not from #21866) so the two batches review independently.

## Badge vs. re-point

Per the [link policy](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/develop/docs/public-docs/op-stack/contribute/link-policy.mdx), a pin is kept and badged only when the pin is the point — upgrade notices quoting the exact rc tag, registry commit, or Makefile revision an operator must build against, and references to source that no longer exists at `develop` (the legacy `L2OutputOracle`, the retired `op-bindings/artifacts.json`) — those got the policy's "as of `x.y.z`" badge form with the tag/sha taken from the pinned URL itself. Everywhere else the pin was an accident of history (guides describing *current* behavior through 2023-era commits and pre-`src/`-layout paths), so the link was re-pointed to the `develop` path: **every re-pointed target was verified to exist at `develop`, and every line anchor was recomputed against the current source** (e.g. `StandardBridge.sol` function ranges, `SuperchainConfig.pause/unpause`, `CrossL2Inbox.validateMessage`, `GasPriceOracle.getL1Fee`, op-batcher `publishingLoop`/`publishStateToL1`). A few re-points also correct the target while keeping the prose claim: `OptimismPortal#L209` links now split into `proveWithdrawalTransaction` (withdrawal proving context) vs `depositTransaction` (sequencer-bypass context), and `challenger.mdx`'s "FaultDisputeGame" bond link now actually points at `FaultDisputeGame.getRequiredBond` instead of `DisputeGameFactory`.

## Per-section counts (95 fixed)

| section | findings | re-pointed | badged |
|---|---|---|---|
| app-developers (guides, tutorials, tools, reference) | 38 | 38 | 0 |
| chain-operators tutorials | 6 | 6 | 0 |
| node-operators reference | 1 | 1 | 0 |
| op-stack (transactions, protocol, security, fault-proofs, features) | 24 | 21 | 3 |
| notices (archive + upgrade-19) | 26 | 0 | 26 |
| **total** | **95** | **66** | **29** |

## Deferred (still baselined, 196 remaining)

*   `op-stack/protocol/smart-contracts.mdx` — 104 pins, deliberately left for its own batch 3 so this PR stays reviewable.
*   `op-stack/bridging/deposit-flow.mdx` + `withdrawal-flow.mdx` — 40 findings held on #21593.
*   Generated `releases/` pages (`op-contracts`, `op-reth`, `op-node`, `kona-node`) — 23 pins that live in release-body content re-fetched by `scripts/generate-releases.ts`; badging the output would be overwritten on regeneration, so these need a generator-level pass (follow-up noted on the tracking issue).
*   Files owned by open PR #21866 (`mips.mdx`, `faq-sec-model.mdx`, `components.mdx`, `overview.mdx`, `fp-components.mdx`, `glossary.mdx`) — 29 pins, swept after that batch merges to avoid cross-PR conflicts.

## Verification

*   Link-policy linter: 0 new findings, 0 stale, with and without `--specs-src`; `--self-test` green.
*   Baseline key-diff: pure removal (0 added, 368 → 273 entries).
*   `lint:nav` OK (395 pages, unchanged), `lint:redirects` OK (22 grandfathered, unchanged), `docs.json` untouched.

**Note:** the baseline file conflicts with #21866 are mechanical; whichever merges second re-runs `--update-baseline`.
